title: AI Data Centers and Environmental Friction
description: Context: Global resistance against the environmental toll of Artificial Intelligence (AI) data centers has intensified significantly. About AI Data Centers and Environmental Friction: Key Data and Statistics On Global & Indian Data Centers: The Imperative Need for Strict Environmental Regulation: Example: The Andhra Pradesh government has granted 15-year power and 10-year water subsidies to massive tech projects, pulling resources from already over-allocated networks. Example: Massive projects are being built on lush orchards, farmlands, and coastal strips that experts warn are already facing severe environmental challenges. Example: Ordinary consumers face rising utility bills and water cutbacks while highly profitable tech giants receive deeply discounted resources. Example: Major developments, like Google’s joint facility, have had their mandatory Environmental Impact Assessments completely waived. Current Global Initiatives vs. Indian Policy: India’s aggressive push to become a global hub for AI data centers overlooks the heavy environmental costs that are fueling protests worldwide. Granting extensive tax holidays and utility subsidies to hyper-scale server farms places a severe burden on the nation’s already strained water tables and electricity grids. Analyse how AI data centres can act as anchors for decentralised renewable clusters. Examine the socio-economic opportunities this presents for semi-urban India. Suggest policy innovations to maximise benefits. (15 M)

title: Sustainable Agriculture in India
description: This editorial is based on “Right time to focus on sustainable agriculture” published in The Hindu Business Line on 12/06/2026. The article emphasizes that India must transition to a climate-resilient, sustainable agricultural framework. It highlights the urgent need to realign support policies, scale R&D funding, and incentivize ecosystem services to secure food stability amidst climate change. For Prelims: Sustainable Agriculture, GMO Seeds, Crop Rotation, Carbon Sink, Drip Irrigation, Dead Zone, Food Chain, Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana, Soil Health Card Scheme, NAFCC, NABARD, National Agriculture Market (e-NAM), Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Carbon Sequestration, Participatory Guarantee System, PM-KUSUM, Seed Bank. For Mains: Key Facts Regarding Sustainable Agriculture, Key Steps Taken to Promote its Adoption in India, Persisting Issues in Adoption of Sustainable Agriculture in India. To address the multifaceted challenges posed by climate change and resource-intensive practices, India must urgently transition toward a resilient agricultural framework that prioritizes sustainability and productivity. There is an urgent need to scale up public and private (CSR-like) funding for R&D and improve technology transfer from "lab to fields." Furthermore, the integration of AI-based weather forecasting models for real-time crop advisory is essential.
